The epitope of IG2 Fab on the ectodomain of HCMV gB (Merlin strain), was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. Mutations were introduced in HCMV gB that allow its secretion as a homogeneous and stable postfusion trimer from mammalian cells. To increase protein secretion, three hydrophobic residues in the fusion loops were mutated with the corresponding more hydrophilic amino acids from HSV-1 gB (I157H, H158R and W240R). The canonical furin cleavage site was mutated to decrease protein heterogeneity caused by incomplete processing during expression, as well as the exposed Cys246 (Cys246Ser) to prevent formation of spurious disulfide bonds. A glycosylation site was introduced in fusion loop-2 (Trp240Asn and Tyr242Thr), predicted to be solvent exposed in the trimer, to interfere with dimerization. To obtain crystals of the IG2/gB complex, the first 63 N-terminal residues were deleted (ΔNgB-glyco construct) and the protein was enzymatically deglycosylated with endoglycosidase H. The asymmetric unit contained one gB monomer bound to IG2 Fab.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 3.6 angstroms

The structure of epitope-specific IG2 Fab in complex with the ectodomain of HCMV gB (Merlin strain), was analyzed by negative stain electron microscopy. Mutations were introduced in HCMV gB that allow its secretion as a homogeneous and stable postfusion trimer from mammalian cells. To increase protein secretion, three hydrophobic residues in the fusion loops were mutated with the corresponding more hydrophilic amino acids from HSV-1 gB (I157H, H158R and W240R). The canonical furin cleavage site was mutated to decrease protein heterogeneity caused by incomplete processing during expression, as well as the exposed Cys246 (Cys246Ser) to prevent formation of spurious disulfide bonds. The mutated protein (gB-698) formed dimers of the characteristic three-lobed postfusion trimers, as determined by size exclusion chromatography (SEC) and negative stain EM. A glycosylation site was introduced in fusion loop-2 (Trp240Asn and Tyr242Thr), predicted to be solvent exposed in the trimer, to interfere with dimerization. Comparison of negative stain two-dimensional class averages of gB-698glyco alone and bound to 1G2 confirmed that all three sites on the gB trimer are occupied by Fab molecules.
